title: Victorian WWCC System Revoked Dozens of Checks for Blacklisted Workers
body: Victoria's Working with Children Check system has stripped dozens of workers of their clearances after they were found on national blacklists. The action follows system improvements to better identify workers who have been barred in other jurisdictions. Sporting clubs should ensure all volunteers and staff have current, valid WWCCs.

title: NSW Bans Appeals for Denied Working with Children Checks
body: NSW has introduced legislation preventing people from appealing decisions to deny or cancel Working with Children Checks. The change aims to close a loophole that allowed unsuitable individuals to delay or overturn negative assessment decisions. This strengthens child safety protections for organisations including sporting clubs.

title: National Continuous Monitoring System for WWCCs in Pilot Phase
body: A new national system to continuously monitor the criminal history of people holding Working with Children Checks is now in pilot testing. The system will provide real-time alerts when WWCC holders are charged with relevant offences across Australia. Full implementation is expected to take several years, but will significantly improve child safety monitoring.

title: NSW Conducting Review of Working with Children Check System
body: The NSW Government is conducting a review of its Working with Children Check system, including consultations with Aboriginal communities. The review examines current processes and seeks feedback on potential improvements. Sporting organisations may have opportunities to contribute feedback during the consultation period.
source: NSW Office of the Children's Guardian

title: Community Sport Volunteers Need Better Child Safety Support
body: New research from The Conversation highlights that community sport volunteers require improved support and resources to effectively safeguard children from abuse. The study points to gaps in training, guidance and practical tools available to volunteer-led sporting clubs. This reinforces the need for clubs to prioritise accessible child safety education and clear safeguarding frameworks.

title: Basketball Australia Launches New Child Safety Resources
body: Basketball Australia has released new child safety resources designed to strengthen safe sport commitments across the basketball community. The resources aim to support clubs and associations in meeting Child Safe Standards and creating safer environments for young participants. Clubs involved in basketball should review these materials to ensure compliance and best practice.

title: WA Announces Crackdown on Working with Children Checks
body: Western Australia will introduce stricter enforcement of Working with Children Check requirements, with stronger penalties for non-compliance. The changes aim to close gaps in the current system and ensure all people working with children hold valid checks. WA sporting clubs should prepare for enhanced compliance monitoring and ensure all relevant volunteers and staff have current WWCCs.

title: Queensland Blue Card Legislative Changes Announced
body: The Queensland Government has announced legislative changes to the Blue Card system that will affect sporting clubs and community organisations. The reforms are expected to strengthen screening processes and compliance requirements for organisations working with children. Queensland clubs should monitor official updates from Blue Card Services for implementation details and timelines.

title: WA: Child Safe Organisations Fact Sheet Released
body: The Western Australian Government has published a fact sheet on child safe organisations. The resource provides guidance for organisations working with children on establishing child safe practices and meeting regulatory expectations. Sporting clubs in WA should review this guidance to ensure compliance with child safety requirements.

title: South Australian Sports Clubs Warned Child Safety Policies May Be 'Worthless'
body: South Australian sports clubs have been given a sobering warning that their child safety policies may be ineffective without proper implementation and cultural change. The warning highlights the gap between having policies on paper and embedding genuine child safe practices across club operations. Clubs should review whether their safeguarding measures are being actively followed and enforced.

title: Motorsport Australia Reinforces Safeguarding and Integrity Framework
body: Motorsport Australia has published information on its safeguarding children and young people framework as part of its integrity commitments. The framework sets out expectations for all participants in motorsport activities to ensure safe environments for children. Motorsport clubs should familiarise themselves with these requirements.

title: QRL Promotes Child Safeguarding Practices for Rugby League Clubs
body: Queensland Rugby League is supporting child safeguarding practices across rugby league clubs in partnership with Sport Community Safety. The initiative provides resources and guidance to help clubs establish safe environments for children and young participants. Rugby league clubs in Queensland should access these safeguarding resources.

title: WA Football Establishes Integrity Unit for Safeguarding
body: WA Football has established an Integrity Unit to handle safeguarding and integrity matters across football in Western Australia. The unit provides a dedicated point of contact for child safety concerns and manages complaints and integrity issues. Football clubs in WA should note the new reporting channels and integrity resources available.

title: Swimming Coach Arrest Highlights Child Safety Concerns in Sport
body: The arrest of a swimming coach in South Australia has raised fresh concerns about child safety practices in children's sports. The case has prompted renewed calls for sporting organisations to strengthen safeguarding measures, background checks and supervision practices. All sporting clubs should review their child protection policies and ensure they have robust screening and monitoring in place.

title: Athletics Australia Emphasises Integrity as Ongoing Cultural Commitment
body: Athletics Australia has reinforced that integrity and child safety are not one-off initiatives but ongoing cultural commitments that require constant attention. The message highlights the importance of embedding safeguarding into everyday club culture rather than treating it as a compliance exercise. Athletics clubs should focus on building and maintaining child safe cultures beyond policy documentation.

title: NSW Children's Guardian Crackdown on Working With Children Check Breaches
body: The NSW Children's Guardian has launched an operation targeting organisations that employ people without valid Working With Children Checks. Sporting clubs in NSW should verify that all volunteers and staff working with children hold current WWCCs and understand their obligations under the scheme.

title: Special Inquiry Criticises NSW Children's Guardian Resources
body: A special inquiry has found that the NSW Children's Guardian's child safe resources are severely deficient or out of date. NSW sporting clubs should be aware that updated guidance and resources are expected to be released, which may affect their child safety compliance requirements.

title: NSW Introduces Independent Early Childhood Regulator
body: NSW will establish an independent early childhood regulator following a review into the sector. While this primarily affects childcare providers, sporting clubs that operate early childhood programs should monitor developments as regulatory changes may extend to other children's services.

title: NSW Office of the Children's Guardian Receives Funding Boost
body: The NSW Government has announced increased funding for the Office of the Children's Guardian to strengthen child safety oversight across sectors including sport and recreation. The funding boost signals tougher compliance monitoring and enforcement activity for organisations working with children. Sporting clubs should ensure their child safe practices and Working with Children Check processes are up to date.

title: NSW Child Safe Standards Now in Effect
body: New child safe standards have commenced in NSW, requiring all organisations working with children to implement comprehensive child safety frameworks. Sporting clubs must meet requirements including child safe recruitment, codes of conduct, complaint handling, and ongoing risk management. The Office of the Children's Guardian has published implementation guidance for organisations.

title: NSW Working with Children Check Reforms Passed
body: The NSW Parliament has passed nation-leading reforms to the Working with Children Check scheme, including continuous monitoring, information sharing between states, and expanded disqualification criteria. The reforms also close a previous loophole that allowed some workers to commence employment before clearances were finalised. Changes will be implemented progressively from late 2025.

title: Child Safe Recruitment Requirements Now Apply in NSW
body: New child safe recruitment and employment requirements are now mandatory for all organisations working with children in NSW, including sporting clubs. Organisations must conduct thorough reference checks, verify Working with Children Checks before employment begins, and document recruitment decisions. The Office of the Children's Guardian has published a recruitment toolkit for organisations.
source: Office of the Children's Guardian NSW

title: NSW Children's Guardian Sacked Following Inquiry
body: The NSW Children's Guardian was removed from office in September 2025 following an inquiry into serious allegations of misconduct. The position oversees Working With Children Checks and child safe standards compliance across NSW, including sporting organisations. Clubs should continue following existing requirements while the Office of the Children's Guardian maintains operations.

title: Sex Offender Found Coaching Without Working With Children Check
body: A registered sex offender was discovered coaching children in NSW without a valid Working With Children Check in July 2025. This case highlights the critical importance of clubs verifying all volunteers and coaches hold current WWCCs before allowing any child-related work. The Office of the Children's Guardian has increased enforcement activity following low compliance rates.

title: Woman Charged With Assault at Sydney Childcare Centre
body: A childcare worker has been charged with assaulting a 10-month-old child at a Sydney centre in June 2026. While this incident occurred in childcare rather than sport, it reinforces the importance of robust child safe practices including supervision, incident reporting and proper screening of all people working with children in any setting.

title: eSafety Commissioner releases new research on cyberbullying in children's sport
body: The eSafety Commissioner has published research exploring cyberbullying and online hate experienced by people connected to children's sports. The report provides insights into the digital challenges facing young athletes, parents, coaches and sporting organisations. This research can help clubs understand and address online safety risks in their communities.

title: National sporting leaders unite to tackle online harm in sport
body: National sporting organisations have joined with the eSafety Commissioner to strengthen efforts against online abuse in Australian sport. The collaboration aims to provide better protections and support for athletes, officials and sporting communities experiencing online harm. Sporting clubs should expect new resources and guidance to emerge from this partnership.

title: New online safety codes introduce protections for children online
body: The eSafety Commissioner has introduced new online safety codes that establish real-world protections for children using digital platforms. The codes set expectations for social media and digital service providers to create safer online environments. Sporting clubs using digital platforms for communication with young members should be aware of these new protective standards.

title: eSafety Commissioner publishes updated guidance on online safety for young people in sport
body: The eSafety Commissioner has released updated resources specifically addressing online safety for young people involved in sport. The guidance covers issues including social media use, image-based abuse, cyberbullying and online harassment in sporting contexts. Clubs can use these materials to support young athletes and their families in navigating online risks.
